solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One reluctant to spend money on phone card during recession

indicators.note: a recession is a going back, so the letters for the words on and phone card are read backwards

parts.note: on means about or concerning, RE
a SIM is the card inside a mobile phone

explanation.surface: A tightwad who won't pay for a phone card while the economy is in a slump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'During recession' looks like economics but signals that the letters go backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A miser hoards money and hates parting with it, the very picture of someone reluctant to spend.

clue.text: I'm upset about brief swaying motion in part of computer

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the letters of I'm upside down, so they read bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written, I and M
C is short for circa, about

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the last letter comes off the word for swaying motion

parts.note: to rock is to sway back and forth
in means fashionable, as does hip

explanation.surface: Someone flustered by a little wobble inside their computer.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upset' turns letters upside down. 'In' is not a container signal but a synonym, fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: The chip of integrated circuitry is a core component of any computer.

clue.text: According to some, has sufficient amount of tobacco

indicators.note: according to some speakers signals that the words are said aloud by people with a certain accent

parts.note: has gives 'S and a sufficient amount is enough, so 's enough

explanation.surface: Some people claim a smoker has enough tobacco.
explanation.walkthrough: ''s enough' said in some regional accents sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Powdered tobacco sniffed up the nose is the traditional form of this product.

clue.text: Terribly arrogant, one's no good as fund-raiser

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters are knocked badly out of order
no says the letter for good is to be left out of the fodder

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral; the 's means one is placed in the mix

explanation.surface: A haughty, useless person makes a poor charity collector.
explanation.walkthrough: Take ARROGANT, drop G (good), add I (one) and rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Rotary Club are known for organising charity fund-raising events.

clue.text: Would-be swimmer is going backwards and forwards for fun

parts.note: a diver is about to enter the water and swim

indicators.note: going backwards means the word is is read in reverse

parts.note: forwards means onwards, ON

explanation.surface: A hesitant swimmer dithering back and forth at the poolside, just for amusement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backwards and forwards' reads as one phrase, but it splits: 'going backwards' is the reversal signal and 'forwards' is a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A diversion is an amusement or pastime, something done for entertainment.

clue.text: Lacking energy, fancy a quick drink

indicators.note: lacking says a letter is missing from the word for fancy

parts.note: to fancy is to dream or imagine
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Feeling tired, someone wants a swift tipple.
explanation.walkthrough: DREAM loses its E.
explanation.definitionFit: A small measure of whisky or spirits, taken quickly, is the Scottish tot.

clue.text: Gallup employee's camera accessory

definitions.meaning: a pollster for the Gallup organisation goes out discovering opinions; the 's stands for is
the eyepiece through which a photographer frames the shot

explanation.definitionFit: Taken literally, the word describes someone who seeks out opinions; normally it is the framing window on a camera.

clue.text: Tabloid editor supporting Republican chief

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means placed beneath, so the editor sits below the Republican

parts.note: top means chief or leading

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor backs a leading Republican politician.
explanation.definitionFit: British tabloid papers are nicknamed for the red mastheads printed at the top of their front pages.

clue.text: Teacher in class with a set of books for RE

parts.note: a form is a school class
NT is the New Testament, a set of books studied in Religious Education

explanation.surface: A schoolteacher in a lesson, holding a stack of textbooks for religious studies.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is Religious Education, a school subject in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: To inform is to pass on knowledge, so one who does so can loosely be called a teacher.

clue.text: Member of family in brownie ceremony

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the phrase brownie ceremony

explanation.surface: A young relative taking part in her Brownie Guides enrolment.
explanation.walkthrough: Brownies are the junior branch of the Girl Guides.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's daughter is a relative, one of the family.

clue.text: Right to accuse criminal in trial

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters are treated wrongly and rearranged

explanation.surface: The right to accuse a criminal during a trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' seems to be the person accused but it is the anagram signal for R, TO and ACCUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal action heard before a judge is a trial in court.

clue.text: Without doubt minor English author

parts.note: defo is British slang for definitely, without doubt
English cut down to a minor form is its abbreviation E

explanation.surface: Undoubtedly a second-rate English writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minor' seems to describe the author, but it shrinks English to E.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel Defoe wrote Robinson Crusoe, making him a celebrated novelist.

clue.text: I'll bring in some wood for burning

indicators.note: will bring in says the letters for wood go inside those for I

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
fir is a kind of timber

explanation.surface: Someone offering to fetch logs for the fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' stands for the numeral one; the 'll joins the surface and signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Something alight and in flames is burning.

clue.text: Odd characters banned from golf links, as expected

indicators.note: removing the first and third letters of golf leaves its even ones

parts.note: golf links are a golf course

explanation.surface: Weird people kept off the golf course, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping G and L from GOLF leaves OF.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means naturally or certainly, just as one would anticipate.

clue.text: Bounder on the carpet, involving girl in illegal substance

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the next piece
involving means taking in, so the girl goes inside the bounder

parts.note: a cad is a dishonourable man, a bounder
a lass is a girl
a rug is a small carpet

explanation.surface: A cad reprimanded for getting a girl mixed up with drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the carpet' suggests being reprimanded; here it puts CLASSAD above RUG.
explanation.definitionFit: UK law sorts drugs into categories, with the most harmful such as heroin in the top one.

clue.text: What caber-tossing adulterer will do?

parts.note: a caber-tosser hurls the pole, a literal fling, while an adulterer indulges in a brief affair

explanation.surface: A wry question about a Highland games athlete who cheats on their spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: A caber is a heavy tree trunk tossed at Scottish Highland games.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase covers both making a throw and indulging in a short affair.

clue.text: French wine old boy knocked back with unusually large curries

parts.note: vin is the French word for wine

indicators.note: knocked back means the letters for old boy are read backwards

parts.note: a lad is a boy
OS stands for outsize, unusually large

explanation.surface: An old boy drinking French wine with enormous curries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' suggests drinking but reverses OLAD to DALO.
explanation.definitionFit: These are fiery hot dishes of Goan origin, a staple of British curry houses.

clue.text: A little orphan demanded help

indicators.note: A little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A small orphan asks for assistance, as in Oliver Twist.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone a hand is to assist them.

clue.text: Noncomformist Norfolk town register

parts.note: Diss is a market town in Norfolk, an English county
to register an item is to enter it in a record

explanation.surface: A town in Norfolk keeps a register of nonconformists.
explanation.walkthrough: Diss is a small market town in Norfolk, in the east of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically, Protestants who refused the Church of England were called Dissenters or Nonconformists.

clue.text: Spotted Gregory being transported in winter?

indicators.note: being transported in means carried inside, so the actor goes inside the vehicle

parts.note: a sled is the transport of winter, with the question mark marking the loose definition
Gregory Peck was the Hollywood actor

explanation.surface: Was the film star seen riding a sleigh in winter?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spotted' seems to mean seen, but it means dotted.
explanation.definitionFit: Something covered in small spots or flecks is dotted.

clue.text: Shipping line going to NY for £25

parts.note: P&O is the well-known British shipping company

explanation.surface: A shipping company offering a crossing to New York for twenty-five pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a pony is twenty-five pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockney money slang gives the sum of twenty-five pounds the name of a small horse.

clue.text: Some practitioners love reorganisation of state hospital? Not half

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, so O

indicators.note: reorganisation means the letters are rearranged
not half says only half of the word hospital is used

explanation.surface: Some doctors would love to see the state hospital reorganised — not half they would!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' looks like the slangy 'very much', but it keeps only the first half of hospital before the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: These are therapists who treat ailments by manipulating bones and muscles, a kind of medical practitioner.

clue.text: Seat of power moved north-east

indicators.note: moved means the letters of north are shifted about

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: The government relocated to the north-east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North-east' looks like a direction, but NORTH is rearranged and E added.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch's ceremonial chair stands for royal authority itself.

clue.text: One's stupid to consume hot drink outside

indicators.note: outside means the drink goes around the other letters

parts.note: mead is a drink made from honey
to eat is to consume
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: It's daft to have a hot drink outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's stupid' means one who is stupid, a noun phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal insult for a dim-witted person, a dolt or idiot.

clue.text: Clean hair standing on end?

parts.note: a mop is a thick mass of hair
something upright stands up

explanation.surface: Tidying a head of hair that's sticking up.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear up a mess or spill is to clean it away.

clue.text: Small portion with last of the pickle

parts.note: a scrap is a small bit

indicators.note: last of means the final letter of the word the

explanation.surface: A little helping with the end of the chutney.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pickle' seems the food but means a predicament.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean an awkward predicament or tight spot.

clue.text: Gas badly affected organ

indicators.note: badly affected means the letters are damaged and jumbled

explanation.surface: A harmful gas damaged a bodily organ.
explanation.definitionFit: This inert noble gas makes up about one per cent of air.

clue.text: Standard recipe for fish

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from the Latin on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A standard method for cooking fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A young salmon in its early river stage has this name.

clue.text: Picasso's tips for framing attractive picture

indicators.note: framing means the tips go around the other letters
the tips of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: hot means sexy, attractive

explanation.surface: Picasso's advice on framing a beautiful painting.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is not a letter, so Picasso's tips are P and O.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a photograph, the everyday short form, is a picture taken with a camera.

clue.text: Come down again, clutching middle of torch as source of illumination

indicators.note: clutching means holding the middle letter inside

parts.note: to alight is to come down, so re-alight is to do it again

indicators.note: middle of means the central letter of the word torch

explanation.surface: Someone landing a second time holding a torch for light.
explanation.definitionFit: The red lamp at the back of a car or bike is a source of light.

clue.text: Traveller about to go on break round loch, proceeding westwards

indicators.note: in an across clue proceeding westwards means reading right to left
to go on means one piece is placed next to the following one

parts.note: re means about, concerning

indicators.note: round means the break goes around the loch

parts.note: a gap is a break
Ness is the famous Scottish loch

explanation.surface: A traveller about to take a holiday around a Scottish loch, heading west.
explanation.walkthrough: RE plus G(NESS)AP gives REGNESSAP, which read westwards is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A person carried by a vehicle is a traveller.

clue.text: Foreign currency not quite enough for Breton resort

indicators.note: not quite enough means the word falls short by its last letter

parts.note: Dinard is a seaside resort in Brittany

explanation.surface: Holiday money doesn't stretch far enough for a trip to Brittany.
explanation.walkthrough: Dinard is a resort on the north coast of Brittany.
explanation.definitionFit: This unit of money is used in several countries, such as Serbia and Jordan.
